subject: Quantify E2E latency gap — hosted vs incumbent (post-call recap & next steps)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@orchid.health>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@orchid.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quantify E2E latency gap — hosted vs incumbent (post-call recap & next steps)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed, minimal plan so we can quantify the p95/p99 end-to-end gap between your current provider and Redwood Hosted: 

Call highlights (brief):
- Orchid needs p95 <= 150ms and p99 <= 400ms for short text generation flows (avg input 30 tokens, output 80 tokens)
- Current provider shows acceptable median but tail spikes during concurrent bursts and streaming sessions
- Key unknowns: concurrency profile, client-side RTT distribution, and whether streaming path is used in-prod for n-best/partial token streaming

Proposed next steps (we can run these in parallel to speed decisioning):
1) You share a representative traffic sample (small CSV) with per-request timestamp, payload size, and a flag for streaming vs non-streaming. I attached a template (orchid_traffic_profile.csv).
2) Redwood runs two micro-experiments:
   a) Synthetic replay with your traffic profile against our Hosted API and your incumbent endpoints to measure p95/p99 server-to-server times (tokenization -> last token emitted).
   b) End-to-end client-shaped test: we route traffic through a lightweight client harness in your region to capture RTT + server tail under realistic concurrency.
3) Establish success gates: p95 <= 150ms and p99 <= 400ms (end-to-end). If Redwood misses by <= 15% on p95 and matches p99, we move to a short pilot; otherwise, we detail remediation (routing tweaks, batching, KV cache warmups, streaming chunking).

Deliverables and timelines:
- Today: I’m attaching the traffic template. Please return a 24–72 hour sample when convenient.
- Redwood will deliver baseline numbers within 3 business days of receiving sample.
- Follow-up call to review results and decide pilot within 2 business days after results.

Attachments: orchard_traffic_profile.csv (template), p95_p99_test_plan.xlsx (test matrix & runbook stub).

Questions or constraints we should explicitly account for? (eg: strict egress routing, SNI pinning, client-side TLS termination, or any EU data residency elements).

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@orchid.health>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@orchid.health>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantify E2E latency gap — hosted vs incumbent (post-call recap & next steps)

Diego —

Thanks for the clear plan and the template. A couple clarifications from our side before we pull the sample: 
- Concurrent profile: 95% of traffic is low-concurrency (1–2 concurrent requests per client), but we have three peak windows where concurrency per client reaches ~8–12 for 30m each. Overall system concurrency across instances averages ~200 during peaks.
- We do use streaming in 40% of sessions to progressively render candidate tokens to the web client. In streaming mode we fragment responses in ~16-token chunks.
- Client RTT: median ~30ms (US-west), 90th ~80ms. We can provide a small synthetic harness for end-to-end runs if helpful.

We’ll pull a 48–72 hour sample from last week and attach it early tomorrow. Quick ask: can your replay harness simulate our streaming chunk sizes and inter-chunk delays so we can see both server tail and perceived client latency?

Regards,
Alex Mercer
Head of ML Systems | Orchid Health
alex.mercer@orchid.health
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@orchid.health>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@orchid.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantify E2E latency gap — hosted vs incumbent (post-call recap & next steps)

Alex —

Yes — we can absolutely model the streaming chunking behavior and inter-chunk delays. Our replay harness supports two modes: pure server-only (measures server emission times) and client-shaped (injects RTT distribution and chunked reads). Please include the client-side observed delays in the CSV, but if not available, we’ll use the RTT distribution you shared (median 30ms / 90th 80ms).

A few practical items:
- Please sanitize any PHI prior to sending. We only need hashed request ids and payload-size indicators — not patient identifiers.
- If procurement will be involved later, loop them in but the technical baseline run is purely scoped to measurement (no contract exchange required).

I’ll kick off internal allocation for the replay and tag Marissa for the runbook. Ben — can you reserve a couple of dedicated nodes for the comparison window (we want isolation from noisy neighbors)?

Thanks —
Diego
From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@orchid.health>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@orchid.health>
Cc: procurement@orchid.health, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantify E2E latency gap — hosted vs incumbent (post-call recap & next steps)

Diego / Alex —

Attached: 48h traffic sample (sanitized) — includes timestamp, request size, streaming flag, and a hashed request id. Also included our internal note about peak windows. We redacted PHI as requested.

Procurement is cc’d for visibility — if Redwood’s numbers look promising we’ll follow procurement steps next week.

Next milestone: we expect Redwood baseline numbers by EOD Monday (18 Aug). Please confirm if that timeline still works for you.

Best,
Priya Rao
Senior Product Ops | Orchid Health
priya.rao@orchid.health
